lessons.title: Not only … but also: Connecting and Emphasizing
lessons.content: 'Not only … but also' is used to connect and emphasize two phrases or two words at the same position. Parallelism should be the goal — the words joined should be the same grammatical type (nouns with nouns, verbs with verbs, adjectives with adjectives).

details.concept: Subject + verb + not only + noun/adj/adv + but also + noun/adj/adv
details.explanation: Place 'not only' before the first item and 'but also' before the second item.
details.example: He can speak not only English but also German.
details.burmese: He can speak not only English but also German.

details.concept: Subject + not only + verb + but also + verb
details.explanation: When joining two verbs, place 'not only' before the first verb and 'but also' before the second.
details.example: She not only dances extraordinarily but also sings perfectly.
details.burmese: She not only dances extraordinarily but also sings perfectly.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Not only … but also
lessons.content: If one subject is singular and the other is plural, the verb form agrees with the subject that is nearest the verb. This rule is the same as with 'either … or' and 'neither … nor'.

details.explanation: When subjects differ in number, the verb takes the form of the nearer subject.
details.example: Not only the bears but also the lion escapes from the zoo.
details.burmese: Not only the bears but also the lion escapes from the zoo.

details.explanation: When the order of subjects is reversed, the verb form may change to agree with the new nearest subject.
details.example: Not only the lion but also the bears escape from the zoo.
details.burmese: Not only the lion but also the bears escape from the zoo.
